subject: noi mistakes that kill deals
preheader: four ways investors overstate noi and regret it later.
headline: Most NOI numbers I see are wrong in the same four ways.
body: Mistake 1: forgetting vacancy. Pro formas show 100% occupancy. The real world is 5-10%. On a $1,800/mo rental, an honest 8% vacancy assumption costs you $1,728/year. Skip it and your NOI is inflated by that amount.

Mistake 2: forgetting property management. Even if you self-manage today, your NOI should reflect a market PM rate (8-10% of gross rent). Otherwise the property's NOI depends on you working for free, and your cap rate is a fiction.

Mistake 3: using gross rent instead of effective gross income. Effective gross = gross rent minus vacancy and credit loss. Skipping this step is the single most common reason a deal looks 9% on paper and lives at 7% in reality.

Mistake 4: ignoring CapEx. Roof, HVAC, water heater, appliances — these aren't optional, they're amortized over 15-20 years. Budget 5-10% of gross rent for CapEx or you'll be surprised twice: once when the roof fails, twice when you realize NOI was wrong all along.
